title: Wolf-Rayet 124 (NIRCam and MIRI composite image)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Webb ERO Production Team

geometryEvidence.reference: A picture of the sky: the plane is the picture's own tangent plane, perpendicular to the sight line through the picture's centre, so it faces the Sun. That centre is 2.0 arcsec from the star, which is the whole of the recipe's inclination. Not the orientation of the nebula.

registration.method: The file's embedded sky tags for scale and direction, 0.0300 arcsec per pixel and north 40.64° right of vertical, and the star for place: the middle of WR 124's saturated pixels, pixel 2271.7, 2195.8, is set at SIMBAD's place for the star, so the frame's centre is 287.8791935°, 16.8604008°. The tags alone put the star 0.21 arcsec from there.

displayModel: Inside the outline of the model of Zavala et al. (2022), each sight line's light lies on two walls: the nearer half of the model's gas along it and the farther half, each at its own middle. The two share the picture's smooth light; its fine detail is on the nearer one. Over the outer tenth of the way from the star to the model's outline the walls are led onto the picture's plane, where the picture outside the outline lies: a presentation choice. The star's own light, out to 5.7 arcsec, stays at the star.
coverage: The published frame inside a circle about the star: the picture fades out between 57.9 and 64.3 arcsec, the largest circle the frame holds, so no straight edge shows.

acquisition.operation: Download the publisher's JPEG; no crop or resample; stars removed by the lab's star remover.
